newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs close at 6-mth high, but Haitai hurts.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs close at 6-mth high, but Haitai hurts.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed at a new six-month high on Wednesday, as foreign buying in heavyweights supported the index, brokers said.
But the immediate shock from rumours of a financial crisis at the Haitai Group hurt shares in companies that have actively expanded their business in recent years, they said.
Banks fell on news that a presidential panel upheld the current ownership limit in banks while construction and securities firms gained on hopes of falling interest rates.
The composite index closed 3.04 points, or 0.41 percent, higher at 737.71, the highest since November 21.
The South Korean market was largely unmoved by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged and the subsequent rallies of most of Asian stock markets.
Haitai, the nation's 24th-largest conglomerate, denied the rumours that it was experiencing financial troubles but shares of the group's three listed affiliates plunged.
Haitai Confectionery Co, flagship of the group, lost 800 won to its daily limit of 10,300. Haitai Electronics Co was down 1,000 won to 11,600 and Haitai Stores Co down 540 won to 6,310.

The banking sub-index shed 2.62 percent or 9.58 points to 356.02 on Monday's news that the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform favoured maintaining the current 4 percent individual ownership ceiling in banks.
The panel had considered raising the ceiling to 10 percent to establish reponsible management in banks and to improve their competitiveness.
Recent interest rate drops and hopes of further falls boosted buying of shares in construction and securities firms, which heavily rely on borrowings, brokers said.
In statements filed later in the day with the Korea Stock Exchange, executives of the three companies said rumours of financial troubles were "totally groundless".

"The Haitai rumours kept the market in the negative territory for most of the day," said Chae Chi-bum, an analyst at Daishin Securities. "But buying regained momentum on talks that foreigners are increasing buying in key blue chips."

Yukong Ltd and LG Chemical and were among the main gainers on foreign buying talks, brokers said. Yukong rose 1,400 won to its daily limit of 19,600 and LG Chemical added 900 won to its limit of 12,500.
The construction sector's sub-index gained 2.29 percent or 6.34 points to 282.63 and that for securities firms added 0.33 percent or 3.47 points to 1,067.55.
The overnight call rates are now at about 12.30 percent, down from about 13.00 percent a week before.
Index futures June contracts closed flat at 75.10 while the underlying KOSPI-200 index gained 0.57 of a point to 75.17.
